modules.title: AGM (Automated Game Matcher: peer challenges + token escrow + stock rewards)
modules.summary: The invented Automated Game Matcher (AGM). Players make or take skill challenges on any native game, with ANY SPL token escrowed, matched maker-to-taker, and the winner rewarded (optionally as tokenized stock). AGM only matches and settles; it never changes gameplay. Revived from docs/architecture-2.0.md, rebuilt non-custodial on the ER (supersedes the earlier base-layer order book).
expectedInput: Locked results from arcv2m2 (the seam) and the match facts from arcv2m12 (the multiplayer rail).
A maker challenge: game tag, SPL token mint (chosen from the embedded wallet or pasted), amount, optional reward mode (stake token, or a chosen tokenized stock), and a window.
expectedOutput: A matched, escrow-locked challenge; on finish, ER settlement: 90% to the winner and 10% platform fee; in stock mode the profit portion is swapped into the chosen stock and priced by the Pyth Lazer oracle.
No platform-paid accounts, no custody by the platform, and no change to the game.
details: WHAT IT IS: the Automated Game Matcher (invented by Solomon Foskaay). A game-agnostic matcher, not a game. Players prove proficiency at a native game by making or taking a challenge, maker/taker like a trading order book. It plugs into the SAME match (arcv2m12) and the SAME result (arcv2m2) and never changes gameplay.

MAKER/TAKER: a maker posts a challenge (game, token mint, amount, optional reward mode, window). It appears on a shared challenges table. Any taker may take it; on take, both stakes are escrowed. EXACT MATCH RULE: the taker must match the exact mint AND the exact amount (1,000 BONK can never take a 5 USDC challenge; a BONK challenge can only be taken with the same BONK amount).
ANY SPL TOKEN: the mint is chosen from the embedded wallet or pasted. USDC, USDT, SOL-wrapped, or a memecoin all work the same; the program validates the mint and the amount.

NON-CUSTODIAL ESCROW (rebuilt): a program-owned eATA (Ephemeral SPL Token program SPLxh1...) per challenge mint, delegated to the ER, with PDA-signed transfers. The platform never holds funds. This supersedes the earlier base-layer order book, which posted orders on base and cost per transaction.

FEE AND AUTO-SPLIT (via arcv2m15): flat 10% of the matched total. Of that fee, 70% goes to the Backer pool (the 100 Early Backer NFTs) and 30% to the platform admin, split atomically in the same settlement. The winner receives their own stake back plus the matched stake minus the 10% fee.

STOCK-REWARD SETTLEMENT (the Stocklana innovation): the reward may be delivered as a tokenized stock (for example AAPLx/TSLx). At settlement the profit portion is swapped into the chosen stock mint and priced by the Pyth Lazer oracle on the ER, so the winner ends with their token AND a stock position. Example: 10 USDC plus 10 USDC, 2 fee, winner gets 10 USDC back plus 8 USDC of stock.
LANGUAGE/FRAMING (HARD RULE): never gambling or betting words. Use make or take a challenge, prove your proficiency, win the reward. Not bet, pot, or wager.
NO PLATFORM OVERHEAD: no platform-paid accounts. The challenge account rent is paid by the maker; the escrow is per challenge; it does not touch the Player Core account (arcv2m3/arcv2m4 redesign).

ON-CHAIN STATE: challenge PDA (seed gfgagm, seq), eATA escrow, optional stock mint, status machine (open -> matched -> locked -> settled/cancelled). ORDERS NEVER EXPIRE (keeps liquidity while P2C is off); the MAKER may cancel their own open order for a full refund of their own deposit. No timer, no crank, no expiry refund.
REUSE: consumes arcv2m12 (match) and arcv2m2 (result seam); the game is unchanged, free play and stake 0 still emit the same envelope.
P2C (availability filler, DEFERRED): the platform bank funds computer seats so a challenge always finds a counterpart. Honest break-even is 55.6%; P2C is never the profit center. Deferred behind P2P.
PROGRAM PLACEMENT: additive on the same gfg program (or a dedicated AGM module program later), NEW seed prefix, versioned layouts, undelegate_* for any new PDA, no live seed change.
REPUTATION: winner reputation keyed to the GFG handle only (never wallet, email, or name). Optional arcv2m9/SOAR records later.
HACKATHON FIT: skill challenges whose prize settles in tokenized stocks on Solana, a consumer/social use of tokenized equities (Stocklana).
DEFERRED: leverage/prop mode, N-way tournaments beyond 2, fiat on-ramp, and the P2C product.

BACKER SHARE: 70% of the AGM fee feeds the Backer pool (config-driven, adjustable). This is the main reason an Early Backer holds and the reason the platform can reach mainnet; it is a share of fees actually collected, so it can never sink the platform.

modules.title: Revenue splitter + Backer pool (automatic, trustless on-chain distribution)
modules.summary: One shared, config-driven splitter that distributes every incoming payment and fee ATOMICALLY in the same transaction via PDA-signed transfers: subscription 20% to the referrer / 30% to the competition escrow / 50% to the admin wallet, and the AGM fee 70% to the Backer pool / 30% to admin. Includes the Backer pool for the 100 Early Backer NFTs with a trustless claim. No manual steps, no platform capital, no one to trust.
expectedInput: A payment or fee event from arcv2m5 (subscription) or arcv2m14 (AGM), with an amount and a split profile key.
expectedOutput: The amount distributed atomically to the configured destinations in the same transaction, plus the Backer pool accrual with a per-holder claim index.
The player is activated in the SAME transaction (subscription) or the match settled (AGM).
details: CONFIG-DRIVEN (basis points, data not code): each split profile lists destinations and bps (subscription profile: 2000 referrer, 3000 competition escrow, 5000 admin; AGM profile: 7000 Backer pool, 3000 admin). Changeable without a program change.

PAYMENT-TRIGGERED ACTIVATION (owner 2026-09-19, FULLY AUTOMATIC): a confirmed USDC payment on Arc is the ONLY key. The relayer watches Arc for the payment tx, verifies it (correct amount, correct recipient, not already consumed), and in the SAME flow splits the money and writes the on-chain activation. The player taps once and is unlocked instantly; there is NO human verification step. HARD GUARD: nothing is activated without a confirmed, un-spent payment tx; a failed, absent, replayed, or wrong-amount payment activates nothing (payment ref = the tx hash is a one-time replay guard).

PAYMENT SOURCE IS THE CHAIN ITSELF: because the gas token is USDC on Arc, a plain USDC transfer is enough; the watcher treats the on-chain transfer as the proof. A third party cannot unlock without actually paying. This is what makes the unlock bypass-proof.
ATOMIC: distribution happens in the SAME instruction that credits/activates, via PDA-signed transfers (no separate settlement tx, no manual step, no window for a bad actor).
NO PLATFORM CAPITAL and no platform-paid accounts: only money actually collected is split; there is never a fixed payout the platform must cover.
BACKER POOL: a single on-chain pool funded by the AGM split. The 100 Early Backer NFTs each equal 1/100 of the pool. The 100 mints are recorded on-chain so ownership is verifiable, not trusted.

TRUSTLESS CLAIM (dividends-per-share accumulator): the pool keeps a cumulative per-share index; each holder stores a checkpoint. Claim is O(1): heldNFTs x (poolIndex - yourLastIndex). A holder can claim any time (daily/weekly/monthly). No loops, no manual sorting, no trust.
TIES: Early Backer also keeps lifetime L3 access; the revenue share counts EVERY NFT held (more NFTs = more shares), while one NFT unlocks lifetime access per account.
REUSE: called by arcv2m5 (subscriptions) and arcv2m14 (AGM); the games and the seam are untouched.
DEPENDENCIES: arcv2m5, arcv2m6, arcv2m7, arcv2m14, arcv2m3 (Player Core), and the ER (gasless, PDA-signed transfers).

modules.title: EVM rail (Arc): chain adapter, contracts, gasless paymaster, batching
modules.summary: The chain-agnostic rail that lets the same web2 experience (email signup, auto wallet, play, earn, never pay gas) run on Arc, Circle EVM L1 where USDC is the gas token. One module list, two rails: every other module keeps its rules and gains a rails entry saying how it is implemented on each chain. Game mechanics, scoring, economics and the UX do not change; only the layer behind the UI is swapped.

FROM the game engines (arcv2m1): deterministic match state plus signed move states (browser), so only the start and the end need the chain.

items: A chain adapter (src/chain/) with ONE interface and two implementations (svm = Solana as today, evm = Arc), selected by a config switch (VITE_GFG_CHAIN).

Arc contracts (evm/): PlayerCore (the ONE per-player account: points, lives, premium, buckets) plus the GFG-BS settlement contracts (per-match co-signed settlement + Merkle window roots + commit-reveal randomness). Gameplay is NEVER per-action: one co-signed settlement per match, folded into one window root. ERC-4337 paymaster wiring is a fallback for user-signed cases only.
A measured Arc Testnet cost report (deploy, per open, per settle, per batch at N=1/20/100/1000, sponsored cost per game), which is the gate for mainnet.
Every other module gains a rails entry (svm live, evm planned/live) with a one-line implementation note. No module is duplicated per chain.

details: GASLESS ON ARC MUST MEAN NO PER-ACTION TRANSACTIONS (owner-locked 2026-09-19): Arc has NO free execution layer (every tx costs USDC gas), so 'gasless' can NEVER be achieved by batching alone. Batching only shrinks the proof; the expensive part is the number of transactions. Measured failure: a per-action Ludo match (openGame + seatUp + beginGame + commitMove per turn + settleGameOrder) cost about 0.10 USDC and about 63 txs. RULE: gameplay (start, every move, turn/game timers, points, lives, in-game assets) runs OFF the chain with session-key signatures, and ONE co-signed settlement per MATCH is written; hundreds of games share this rail. The player always signs nothing and pays nothing; the relayer sponsor pays the single tiny per-match gas. ARC-4337 paymaster wiring is therefore a fallback for user-signed cases, NOT the mechanism that makes gameplay free.

PLAYERCORE (owner 2026-09-18): ONE contract per chain holding each player's lives, points, premium and per-game buckets, keyed by address, mirroring the Solana Player Core (one account per player, not one account per feature per game). Matches and randomness are separate on purpose (shared services), exactly like the Solana board accounts and the shared VRF.

CHAIN PORTABILITY MAP (must be approved before Phase 0): per module, how the Solana account model maps to EVM. Game rules, scoring, tiers, competition rules and the UX do not change; only the implementation does.

GASLESS (owner decision 2026-09-18): the APP pays the tiny USDC gas directly through its own self-hosted relayer. No paid third-party sponsorship plan (Dynamic sponsorship, Alchemy Gas Manager, Pimlico) is required. An ERC-4337 paymaster is optional later, never a dependency. The player never holds or pays gas. Goal: as cheap as MagicBlock ER or cheaper, because we run ONE relayer instead of many per-player accounts.
RANDOMNESS: Arc has no on-chain randomness (PREVRANDAO returns 0). One seed is committed per batch and revealed at settle; each roll is hash(seed, gameId, counter). No per-roll randomness cost.
MOVES: off-chain signed states (free). Only start and end touch the chain. A short dispute window protects players.

BATCHING: opens and results are collected into Merkle roots; one transaction commits many games (O(1) gas). Settlement flushes on N games OR T minutes, whichever comes first, and stays per-game (immediate) while volume is low, so a match is verifiable within about a minute at launch and batched only at scale. Target about 0.0001 USD per game, roughly 1 USD per tens of thousands of games.
MAX GAME TIME: every game carries deadline = start + MAX_TTL. After it, expire(gameId) is permissionless, so abandoned games never grow the tree. No cron.
NO VERCEL COMPUTE: the game engine runs in the browser; Vercel stays static hosting plus the existing thin endpoints. Batch submission is permissionless.
CONTRACT SIZE: 24 KB per contract (EIP-170), so contracts are split by module concern.
DECIMALS: Arc native USDC is 18-decimal while the ERC-20 view is 6-decimal. One canonical accounting rule, never mix the two.
BRANCH: built on osv1Arc. The agent pushes osv1Arc only; the owner opens the PR to main and approves go-live.

PHASES (build order, not modules): Phase 0 scaffold plus local tests; Phase 1 one Ludo match on Arc Testnet plus measured cost; Phase 2 gasless paymaster plus sponsored cost; Phase 3 batching plus TTL plus scale cost; Phase 4 viability report; Phase 5 mainnet deploy and flip each module rails.evm to live.
RESEARCH SOURCE: the fee findings live in the Research library (/changelog/research.html, research/arc). This module holds the build.

modules.title: GlobalFolkGames Batched Settlement (GFG-BS): Merkle roots + commit-reveal randomness
modules.summary: The platform's OWN settlement layer, built from scratch so no hosted service is required. A MATCH is played OFF the chain (session-key signed moves); at the END, ONE transaction per match carries the whole match (both players' co-signed summary: start, moves hash, finish order, points, timers, result), so the chain sees very little and a match costs near zero. Many matches (and later competitions, trades, posts) are then committed as ONE Merkle root per window. Naming is deliberately precise: this is NOT a rollup (there is no off-chain VM and no state-transition proof); the established terms are batched settlement (Merkle-root commitment) plus commit-reveal randomness, with a session registry and a sponsored relayer. Shown in games as the full project name, shortened to GFG-BS in docs. Standalone on purpose: Arc serves finance, not games, so other game projects can reuse it.

items: FROM a game (any arcv2m1 game): a match id, the players, and the match result with points, plus a deadline (max game time).
FROM the app relayer: the batched roots to publish (opens and settles) and the committed dice seed for the window.
FROM the owner: the window policy N (games) and T (seconds), which are config, not code.
ONE on-chain action per settlement window covers unlimited moves, dice rolls and point writes inside, so the per-game cost falls as 1/N and new features do not add per-action cost.

Provable randomness: one seed committed BEFORE play and revealed at flush; every roll is hash(seed, gameId, counter), free and verifiable, with no per-roll fee (Arc has no on-chain randomness, so this is required).
Bounded growth: every match carries a deadline and can be expired by anyone after it, so abandoned games never grow the tree.
Per-game proofs: each match gets its own Merkle proof against the published root, plus an instant app-signed receipt so the player sees something immediately.
A self-hosted relayer (no paid sponsorship platform) that pays the tiny USDC gas. The player never signs and never pays.

details: NAME + SCOPE: GlobalFolkGames Batched Settlement (GFG-BS), module arcv2m17. In games the full project name is shown; docs may shorten it to GFG-BS. It is NOT a rollup: there is no off-chain VM and no state-transition proof. The accurate, existing technical terms are: MERKLE-ROOT BATCH SETTLEMENT (many signed events committed as one root, each verifiable by a Merkle proof), COMMIT-REVEAL RANDOMNESS (seed committed before play, revealed at close), a SESSION REGISTRY with TTL, and a SPONSORED RELAYER for gasless writes. Standalone on purpose so it can be reused by other game projects; arcv2m16 is the Arc-specific wiring.

GAMEPLAY SETTLEMENT RULE (owner-locked 2026-09-19, HARD): gameplay actions are NEVER individual transactions. During a match the move list, turn clocks, dice derivations and points are computed and held OFF the chain, signed by the players' session keys (no wallet popups, player pays nothing). The chain receives ONE settlement per MATCH at the end, co-signed by BOTH players' session keys, carrying: game tag, match ref, the hash of the full move sequence, the finish order, the points to bank, the elapsed/turn timing, and the result. The relayer submits the already co-signed summary and only pays the tiny gas; it never decides the truth. Nobody can fake a result because a settlement is only valid with both co-signatures. DISPUTE (commit-reveal): only the hash is on-chain at settlement; if either side disputes within the dispute window, the full move list is revealed and the chain re-verifies it against the committed hash. No dispute = no reveal = no extra cost. This applies to EVERYTHING: game start, moves, turn timers, game timers, point awards, lives and in-game assets (hundreds of games share this one rail). The per-action instructions (openGame/seatUp/beginGame/commitMove/expireTurn/settleGameOrder as separate txs) are DEPRECATED for gameplay; they are retained ONLY until per-match settlement replaces them, so no path may ship that charges per action.

MECHANISM: the relayer flushes when the pending batch reaches N games OR the window reaches T seconds, whichever comes first, and always flushes at window close even with one game. Nothing is watched manually and an empty window costs nothing.

COST SHAPE (CORRECTED 2026-09-19 after the live cost test): the Merkle root is NOT what makes the platform cheap on its own. The things that make it cheap are (a) NOT writing every gameplay action to the chain, and (b) batching the per-MATCH settlements. A match is played off the chain with session-key-signed moves; ONE transaction per match settles it (both players co-sign the summary), then many match settlements are folded into ONE commitBatch root per window. Measured truth: a commitBatch transaction is O(1) gas (about 29,000) no matter how many games it carries, BUT a per-ACTION design (openGame + seatUp + beginGame + commitMove-per-turn + settleGameOrder) costs about 63 transactions and 0.10 USDC per 2P match, which is NOT sustainable (a free player at 5 matches/day would cost about 0.50 USDC/day, and 100 such players about 50 USDC/day). The per-action design is DEPRECATED for gameplay: game start, every move, turn timers, finish, points, lives and in-game assets must NEVER be individual transactions. Target shape: 1-2 transactions per MATCH (approximately 0.002-0.004 USDC), so 100 free players at 5 matches/day cost about 1-2 USDC/day total.

BUILT + MEASURED (Arc Testnet, 2026-09-18): contracts GameRegistry 0xC0d3c8...11eb, Randomness 0xb40629...9E23, PlayerCore 0xcebA2d...56cc. Full sponsored game 0.011034 USDC unbatched; 25 forge tests pass. See the Test results workspace (/changelog/tests.html).

RECEIPTS: instant app-signed receipt at game end (with the pre-committed dice-seed hash), then an on-chain receipt at flush with the batch transaction hash and the game's Merkle proof. A config knob can anchor each start on-chain for an instant explorer link at about 0.00243 USDC per game.

SCOPE IS NOT ONLY GAMEPLAY: it settles any signed event, not just match records, so competitions, trades, posts and future features all use the same roots. WHY IT DOES NOT GROW WITH FEATURES: new games, timers, competitions, card trading, forum posts and AGM all become LEAVES or event payloads inside the same windows, so they do not create new per-player accounts and do not add per-action cost. Only a program upgrade (a deploy) costs, which is a one-time cheap transaction.

MAINNET: stay on Arc Testnet until the existing games run on Arc with points, single-player, multiplayer, live and pro subscriptions all working. Then deploy to mainnet (gas only, no rent, no per-player account).
RESEARCH + RESULTS: fee findings live in the Research library; the measured build evidence lives in the Test results workspace.

TERMINOLOGY LOCK (owner 2026-09-18): never call this a rollup. Use "batched settlement" for the Merkle-root commitment mechanism, "commit-reveal randomness" for the dice, "session registry (TTL)" for match start/end, and "sponsored relayer" for gasless writes. Full project name in games; GFG-BS allowed in docs.

MATCH START IS COMMITTED ON-CHAIN (owner-locked 2026-09-19): every real match opens with ONE small transaction that records the players, the match id, a starting commitment and the timeout clock. This gives every match a permanent on-chain beginning (so 'he never started' can never be claimed) and is where the LIFE is charged (charge-at-start, non-refundable). Cost: one small tx; a match is therefore about 2 txs total (start + settlement).

SIGNING IS AUTOMATIC VIA SESSION KEYS (beginner view): the player never manually signs a result. On sign-in the wallet issues a session key; each device signs ITS OWN running view of the match (a hash of the move list) silently, with no popups, exactly like the Solana session-key model today. A tampered move list breaks the signature, so the frontend can never forge a result.

SETTLEMENT IS CO-SIGNED BUT THE LOSER CANNOT BLOCK IT: the normal path is both devices sign an agreeing summary and settlement is instantly final. If either side disagrees or refuses, the match does NOT hang: it escalates to a DISPUTE and the full move list is revealed. The outcome is then decided from the moves and the rules, never from who was willing to sign.

DISPUTE = REVEAL + REPLAY (game-agnostic): the revealed move list is a sequence of state SNAPSHOTS (after move 1, after move 2, ...). Each game supplies its own rule-checker, but the dispute machinery is identical for every game, so it scales to 100+ games. On-chain replay re-applies the moves and computes the winner in the contract; nothing is trusted from either player.

ON-CHAIN REPLAY SCOPE AT LAUNCH (owner-locked 2026-09-19): on-chain rule replay ships for the MONEY games FIRST (Ludo now, then chess, then AGM staked challenges). Casual/free games settle by both-signatures; a disagreement on a casual game falls back to a short review window until that game gets its own replayer. The dispute machinery is identical for all games; only the number of games with a full on-chain replayer grows over time.

ABANDON / NO-SIGNATURE IS HANDLED BY THE CLOCK, NEVER BY A HANG: the match has a timeout window. If play stops, the active side submits a TIMEOUT CLAIM which settles it as a forfeit (one signature, because the clock is objective and already committed at start). If nobody acts at all, the match EXPIRES after the window with no settlement and no points. Because the life is charged at start, abandoning is already a loss, so it is never a free escape.

BATCH WINDOW (owner-locked 2026-09-19, hybrid, config-driven): the relayer flushes when EITHER 100 matches are pending OR the oldest pending match is 1 hour old, and it SKIPS EMPTY WINDOWS (no pending matches = no flush = zero cost). Both numbers are config data (BATCH_MAX=100, BATCH_MAX_AGE=1h), so scaling later is a config edit, never a redeploy. WHY: a plain hourly schedule would flush 24x/day even with 1-5 games, costing ~0.014 USDC/day of pure overhead; skipping empty windows makes cost track ACTUAL PLAY. Measured (20 Gwei): a batch flush is ~29,000 gas = ~0.00058 USDC O(1), so 1 match in an hour costs 0.00058, and 2,400 matches/day costs ~0.014/day. Launch reality (1-5 games/day) is ~0.0006-0.009 USDC/day, under the 0.01/day target. CRITICAL: START COMMITS ARE BATCHED TOO, so both the beginning and the end of a match are committed in the window flush, not as per-match txs. A match's on-chain record appears at window close (up to 1h, or sooner at 100 matches); the app-signed receipt at game end stays INSTANT, and the match-history panel shows 'pending flush' until the batch tx lands.

DISPUTE IS GASSLESS AND COSTS THE PLAYER NOTHING (owner-locked 2026-09-19): a dispute is NOT a separate transaction and there is NO dispute fee. A disagreeing player's device signs a tiny 'dispute' event and appends it to the same off-chain log, exactly like a move (zero gas). The dispute rides inside the same batch flush at no extra per-player cost. The REPLAY (re-applying the moves to decide the true winner) runs OFF-CHAIN, for free, by the verifier, and only when the two devices' digests actually differ; its result is then batched too. So a disputed match still costs the platform only its share of the same window flush. Players are NEVER asked to pay a bond or a fee to dispute.

WHAT A FLUSH ACTUALLY COMMITS (owner-locked 2026-09-19): a flush stores ONE Merkle root. Each MATCH is ONE leaf (gameId + moveDigest + resultHash + moveCount); the batch tx sends only the root, count and block range, so gas is O(1) regardless of N. VERIFIABILITY IS TWO-LAYER: (a) ALWAYS verifiable - the match existed, who played (MatchStarted event), its move count, its result digest, and that the digest carries BOTH players' signatures (so no one can forge a result); membership in the root is provable with a Merkle proof. (b) VERIFIABLE ON DEMAND - the actual move list is OFF-chain but bound to the signed digest, so it becomes checkable the moment it is revealed (the dispute/reveal path). Nothing is 'trust me': the chain permanently commits players + move count + result + both signatures.

FLUSH TIMING IS PER-MATCH, NOT PER-CLOCK-HOUR (owner-locked 2026-09-19): every match starts its OWN 1-hour timer when it finishes; a flush happens when 100 matches are pending OR the OLDEST pending match reaches 1h, and empty windows never flush. A match is swept by the NEXT flush after it finishes, so an overlapping match is never charged twice and never waits a full hour if a flush already happened. COST IS PER FLUSH, never per match and never per move: games in the same burst share ONE flush. Rule of thumb: one flush per BURST of play. Launch reality (3-5 games in a few bursts) is about 0.0006-0.002 USDC/day, under the 0.01/day target.

LIVES MUST REFRESH AT GAME START, NOT AT COMPLETION (owner 2026-09-19): the chain charges the life at game start (non-refundable). The FRONTEND must re-read and re-render the lives meter IMMEDIATELY after the start charge resolves, so the player sees 1 life deducted the moment the game starts. Relying on the match-completion seam to refresh is a BUG: it makes lives appear to drop late (or double) only when a later match completes. This is game-agnostic: the refresh lives in the lives module + the settlement rail, never in one game.

DASHBOARD FLUSH VISIBILITY (owner 2026-09-19): the Arc dashboard shows the batch window state - pending count, the next flush trigger (100 matches or 1h), the time remaining ('in Xm') or 'none' when nothing is pending, and the last flush tx. This is a READ-ONLY display (no gas, no USDC) so it costs nothing and proves the flush timer works before mainnet.

modules.title: Foskaay Gasless Games Infrastructure (standalone, any game plugs in)
modules.summary: A STANDALONE project (its own contracts, its own deploy) that any game plugs into: open a session on-chain, do everything inside for free, settle back once. It is the Arc (Circle EVM) equivalent of MagicBlock's Ephemeral Rollup. Game-type-agnostic: a Ludo board, an idle game's plots and streets, and an MMORPG's galaxy are all the same to the rail - participants, an opaque state model the game defines, signed events, one settlement. The benefit: players never pay gas and never see a wallet popup; the sponsor pays a tiny fixed fee per SESSION instead of per action, so an on-chain game can be as cheap to run as a web2 backend. GlobalFolkGames is its FIRST user, not its purpose. Long-form working note: docs/foskaay-ggi-spec.md (staff/repo only, not served).

items: CORE (4 contracts, unopinionated): SessionRegistry (open/close a session; participant authorities; session-key scope+expiry), SessionState (accept signed events: opaque payload + sequence number + digest), Randomness (commit-reveal seed(s), used only when a game asks), FeeVault (per-session fee + configurable destination).

A session model with 1..N participants and per-participant signing authority set at OPEN, so a tampered client cannot act as another participant (an AI/house seat simply has the relayer key as its authority).
FREE work inside a session: nothing is written to the chain during play (no per-action, no per-move, no per-feature cost). Cost appears on OPEN and SETTLE only.

Commit-reveal randomness: one seed sealed before play, stored as a LIST so a game may declare more independent streams; every in-session random value is derived as hash(seed, counter), free and verifiable after reveal.
A fee per session, charged on DEVNET TOO to the owner wallet, so a developer sees the true mainnet economics before committing. Fees are per session, never per action, so cheapness is preserved.
Packages a developer installs (@foskaay/ggi-sdk, @foskaay/ggi-contracts-sdk): integrating is install + a small per-game adapter + the four calls. Never a fork, never a contract copy.

OPTIONAL PATTERNS (offered, never enforced; core stays exactly 4 contracts): Batched Settlement (a SEPARATE BatchedSettlement contract: submit a session digest into a window, PERMISSIONLESS flush into one Merkle root, Merkle-proof verify; the DEV sets the window size/duration, e.g. 10 games/35min or 1000/24h), Managed Accounts (PlayerCore-style single account per player), Verifiers (per game), House/relayer as a participant.

details: APPROVED 2026-09-21 by the owner. NOT built: Step 1 (empty skeleton foskaay-ggi/ + README + foundry.toml) is the only thing that exists. Step 3 (code) is PENDED pending owner go.

NAMING (owner 2026-09-21): the product is 'Foskaay Gasless Games Infrastructure'. The name sells the BENEFIT (gasless play, cheap for the sponsor), not the mechanism. 'Batched Settlement' is now ONE OPTIONAL PATTERN, not the product; 'Session Rails' is retired as a name. Short form 'Foskaay GGI' is internal only, after the full name has appeared. npm: @foskaay/ggi-sdk, @foskaay/ggi-contracts-sdk. NEVER call it an 'ER' - MagicBlock's ER is an SVM runtime; this is a session/settlement layer on EVM.

CORE vs OPTIONAL IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE (owner 2026-09-21): MagicBlock's rail is deliberately unopinionated and hands devs primitives. Foskaay GGI must do the same. CORE makes NO decision for the game; OPTIONAL patterns are GFG's own opinions, offered as examples only. A dev who wants a separate account per player per feature and a commit every turn must be able to do that and pay more if they like - that is their cost to optimise. Our job is to make the FLOOR ridiculously cheap, not to dictate usage.
CORE CONTRACTS = 4: SessionRegistry, SessionState, Randomness, FeeVault. Nothing else is required to ship a gasless game. Each stays well under the EVM 24KB cap.

OPTIONAL PATTERNS: (a) Batched Settlement - fold many session settlements into one Merkle root per window; cadence is the DEV's choice, never forced to 100/1h; (b) Managed Accounts - the PlayerCore-style single account per player with slots for every game/feature (a cost optimisation, not a mandate); (c) Verifiers - a per-game referee that replays a dispute; only games carrying money truly need one; (d) House/relayer as a participant - only games with an AI or house opponent need it.

WHY STANDALONE: GlobalFolkGames cannot launch on mainnet without it, and other game devs must be able to use it without touching GlobalFolkGames. It deploys its own contracts and GlobalFolkGames calls into it; the game owns its economy, the rail owns the room.

LAW 1 - THE RAIL NEVER LEARNS A GAME CONCEPT: no board, token, position, seat count, turn or dice in the rail. The game's state is an opaque payload. A real-estate grid, a war zone and a galaxy are all equal.

LAW 2 - ACCOUNT LAYOUT IS THE DEV'S CHOICE, BUT UPGRADES ARE SAFE: GFG's own optimisation was one account per player with per-game buckets (version FIRST, new fields LAST, permissionless idempotent migrate_* in the SAME deploy, never init_if_needed onto a changed seed, so an upgrade never touches or orphans a player's points). That is an OFFERED pattern, not a requirement. The rail must also support one-account-per-feature devs without modification.

NO CO-SIGNING (corrected 2026-09-21): the earlier design required BOTH players to co-sign a settlement. MagicBlock does not do this, solo play has no second signer, and it was the source of the recent blocker. Correct model: each participant signs their OWN actions with their own session key (silent, no popups); the contract enforces per-participant authority.

ECONOMICS (modelled on MagicBlock, who charge for sessions + commits, not usage): a small fixed fee per session on open and settle. The owner takes 100% at first; a protocol/node split can come later only if dedicated infrastructure is added. GlobalFolkGames PAYS like any other game because it is the proof of concept and the battle test. Players always pay nothing.

TERMINOLOGY MAP (honest): MagicBlock delegate -> OPEN session; free ER execution -> signed off-chain session state; commit -> SETTLE (or a dev-chosen commit); undelegate -> session close; session key -> session key; ER VRF -> commit-reveal seed; commit batching -> an OPTIONAL Merkle window. The EFFECT ports; the MECHANISM differs because Arc has no delegation program.

WHAT IS THE FAST LAYER (the question every dev asks): MagicBlock runs a fast copy of the SVM (10ms slots) over DELEGATED accounts, free inside, pushing state back to Solana base on COMMIT (that is where cost appears); 'ephemeral' because the rollup's own state is temporary and only committed state is permanent, which is why their fees are for sessions + commits. ER txs do not appear on normal explorers because explorers index the base chain; MagicBlock runs its own endpoints/explorer. Foskaay GGI does the SAME EFFECT on Arc more simply: there is NO ER on Arc and we do not pretend otherwise - nothing to run (no validator/RPC/rollup node); the fast layer is SIGNED session state (free, because not a transaction); at settlement the digest (and whatever the dev commits) is written permanently to Arc base. A tampered action breaks the signature, so a fake result cannot settle. Honest limits: the middle is signed state, not a live parallel VM (no third-party mid-session reads); settlement is submitted by a relayer that is trusted for TIMING, never for TRUTH; and we must ship our own session reader/explorer for visibility.

WHY A DEV MIGHT PICK Foskaay GGI OVER MAGICBLOCK ER: it works on EVM (Arc) where ER cannot run; gas is a stablecoin (USDC) not a volatile token; there is no infrastructure to operate; the shape is familiar (open, free work, settle) so porting is conceptual; and the fee is PER SESSION, not per commit, so a heavy game is not punished.

BUILD ORDER: CORE first only - (1) skeleton DONE; (2) SessionRegistry + SessionState + session keys, tested with a fake game; (3) Randomness (N streams) + FeeVault. Then OPTIONAL patterns when a game asks: Batched Settlement, Managed Accounts, Verifiers (Ludo first); then plug Ludo in as the first real user; then points, lives, premium as event/slot types; later competitions + AGM + ERC-20. Every step ends with a LIVE Arc testnet proof before the next step starts.

RELATION TO arcv2m17: arcv2m17 stays the IN-APP settlement module (Merkle windows + commit-reveal inside GlobalFolkGames). arcv2m18 is the STANDALONE infrastructure that GlobalFolkGames (and any other game) plugs into. They are separate on purpose; do not merge them.

FEES + COST (owner 2026-09-22): Foskaay GGI charges a small FIXED fee PER SESSION, never per action, so a heavy game costs the same as a light one. Two stages: once at OPEN and once at SETTLE (an abandoned session pays only the open fee). The fee is charged in USDC (Arc's native asset and gas token) via the ERC-20 interface; the fee amount is CONFIG on FeeVault (one setFees call, no redeploy) and the SDK READS it at runtime so no number is ever hardcoded. The settle price is LOCKED at open, so an owner fee change can never alter a session already in flight. The fee lands in the FeeVault and only its owner can withdraw it to a configurable destination (for mainnet: a separate cold owner wallet, not the hot relayer). MEASURED ON ARC TESTNET: 4 core contracts total deploy 0.079359 USDC; a realistic batched session is about 0.00002 USDC of Arc gas. COMPARISON (honest, at a standard $100/SOL): MagicBlock's model bills a delegation session (0.0003 SOL) plus each commit (0.0001 SOL), so a match with one session + two commits is 0.0005 SOL = about $0.05. On Arc the same shape costs about $0.00002 of Arc gas plus Foskaay GGI's own per-session fee (placeholder 0.0015 USDC, owner-set), i.e. roughly $0.0015 all-in, and it is priced in a stablecoin rather than a volatile token. MagicBlock is a leader in gasless gaming on Solana and Foskaay GGI does not claim to replace it: Foskaay GGI delivers the same EFFECT on EVM/Arc (where ER cannot run), with no validator, RPC or rollup node to operate, so a dev measures true mainnet economics on testnet instead of guessing. PRICING IS NOT FINAL: the per-session fee is the owner's decision and is intentionally left open so the SDK ships zero hardcoded price.

DEPLOYMENT + UPGRADEABILITY (owner 2026-09-22): the rail is UPGRADEABLE via UUPS proxies (ERC1967, OpenZeppelin). The PROXY addresses are PERMANENT, so improving the logic never moves an address and never strands an open session or any data - this is the lesson from the publishing-first test, where a fresh deploy would have orphaned everything. ARC TESTNET (chain 5042002) proxy addresses: SessionRegistry 0x5165809149Be8A72c72EedBa6a13d57014Ba1bE5, SessionState 0x34945e897Ec9a5CC4ab41d78c8ABe3B5034C5c8e, Randomness 0x6DD15cf4d4E2D29dd4AA871d6fd012221212B38b, FeeVault 0x4cf542791faeb683f878bd3d119683e0C02F9905, BatchedSettlement (optional) 0x5831E31789cAD85Dd263Ec78D73D8289FDc523c4. MAINNET addresses appear in the same shape once deployed; mainnet does NOT start until testnet is battle-tested. The public docs page (/foskaay-ggi/docs/) and the npm packages (@foskaay/ggi-contracts-sdk) carry the same address list.

UPGRADE SAFETY RULE (hard, locked 2026-09-22; ANY agent touching these contracts MUST obey): (1) STORAGE IS APPEND-ONLY - never reorder, rename or remove a state variable, including the uint256[20] __gap and the version marker; new variables consume from the top of the gap and the gap shrinks by the same number of slots, because a reorder reads live data as garbage. (2) Initialization goes through initialize() (re-init guarded); the implementation contract is _disableInitializers() so it can never be used directly; logic-only upgrades must NOT bump version, layout changes MUST. (3) ALWAYS run the upgrade-safety tests (foskaay-ggi/test/UpgradeSafety.t.sol prove the address is kept and data is preserved) and the full suite before any deploy. (4) AFTER every upgrade, REPORT to the owner: proxy address unchanged, open sessions and data checked to still read correctly, the tx, and the new logic version/summary. (5) Upgrade authority is the owner now; it must move to a timelock or multisig BEFORE mainnet, because a single key that can silently repoint the logic is a trust risk on a rail other devs build on. (6) A game dev who wants real immutability can deploy their own instance; the shared rail stays upgradeable so a bug can be fixed for everyone.

Foskaay GGI Midchain FINDING (owner approved 2026-09-22): the Generals port exposed that the current cores do not deliver this module's own promise of free work inside a session. Every move was a separate Arc transaction, so a match cost about 10 games per 1 USD instead of about 1000. The missing piece is the Foskaay GGI Midchain: moves signed with EIP-712 and hash-chained off-chain, executed for free via eth_call on the game's own pure rules, with only two on-chain transactions per match (handover + settle). See the Findings and tables below, the Research library entry ggi-Foskaay GGI Midchain, and foskaay-ggi/foskaay-ggi-build-guide-v5.md section 9.

EVM TECH ARC INHERITS THAT WE HAD NOT USED (owner 2026-09-22): Arc is Osaka baseline, so EIP-7702 (set-code), EIP-1153 (transient storage) and deterministic instant finality are available; EIP-4844 blob transactions are REJECTED. The key primitive is eth_call free execution (run pure game rules without a transaction), plus EIP-712 signatures and a keccak256 hash chain. Together they are the EVM equivalent of MagicBlock's free ER execution.

CORE IMPACT (owner 2026-09-22): the Foskaay GGI Midchain needs NO core contract change. The existing 4 core + 1 optional structure stands: SessionRegistry (open/close/session keys/canSign), SessionState (commitDigest/sealFinal), Randomness (commit-reveal seed) and FeeVault (per-session fee) already cover the on-chain endpoints. The Foskaay GGI Midchain lives in the GAME's own contract (pure getInitialState/applyMove/isTerminal) plus the client/SDK (EIP-712 signing + hash chain) plus an untrusted relay cache. Keep 4 core + 1 optional; do not merge.

Foskaay GGI Midchain PROTOTYPE MEASURED (owner 2026-09-22, Arc testnet): GeneralsMidchain (pure rules, deployed 0x67E2508459Ef1d786C93b30Df7FC922198b0D0b2) + scripts/foskaay-ggi-midchain-match.mjs. Every move runs free via eth_call and is signed + hash-chained off-chain; the verifier replay PASSED. Cost per match: on-chain-board port 0.098172 USDC (about 10 games/$1), Foskaay GGI Midchain unbatched 0.012206 USDC (about 81 games/$1), Foskaay GGI Midchain batched 3-matches-per-window 0.009788 USDC (about 102 games/$1). The remaining cost is the CORE's storage writes at open and settle, not the moves; the v5 target of about 1000 games/$1 needs an event-only handover/settle in the core (future change) and/or larger batches. 143/143 forge tests pass.

EVENT-BASED Foskaay GGI Midchain + BATCH TESTED (owner 2026-09-23, Arc testnet): the event-based form of the Foskaay GGI Midchain (EventMidchainCore, deployed 0x197DE9813bd8cF668C8C26455329C629EE9Fc63e) emits the handover/settle as EVENTS instead of STORAGE, and its handoverMany/settleMany put MANY games in ONE transaction. It is still the Foskaay GGI Midchain (neither fully on base nor offchain; event-based, not offchain). The game link is INSIDE the Handover event (sessionId + gameLogic + startHash + players + sessionKeys), so no separate setGameState tx is needed (2 txs per game, not 3) and the Foskaay GGI explorer can index it directly from eth_getLogs. Measured per game: unbatched 0.001712 USDC (about 584 games/$1); batched 3 = 0.001098 (about 910); batched 5 = 0.000939 (about 1,064); batched 10 = 0.000820 (about 1,219); batched 100 = 0.000713 (about 1,403). The storage-based Foskaay GGI Midchain stays flat under batching (about 102 to 113 games/$1) because each game still pays a per-game SSTORE open. So the event-based Foskaay GGI Midchain + batching CROSSES the v5 target of $1/1000 at just 5 games per batch. 148/148 forge tests pass.

CORE + SDK ADJUSTMENT PROPOSAL (owner 2026-09-23, NOT built; needs explicit approval): CORE (no new address): add event-based handover/handoverMany/settle/settleMany to the EXISTING core via a UUPS logic upgrade (same proxy address, append-only storage) plus ONE new nullifier mapping (sessionId => settled) to stop double settlement; storage-based sessions stay as they are, nothing merged, no data moves. SDK (republish, no chain change): add handover/handoverMany/settle/settleMany/signMove/verifyMidchain helpers. BATCHING STAYS OPTIONAL: the dev chooses unbatched (instant on-chain per game) or batched (cheaper, event lands with the batch); the rail never forces a cadence. The Foskaay GGI explorer shows each game individually in a batch and proves the Foskaay GGI Midchain by replaying the signed moves against the on-chain hashes.

BATCHING ECONOMICS, MEASURED (owner question 2026-09-23): why 5 games batched already gives about 1,064 games per 1 USD but 100 games only about 1,403, not millions. There is NO hidden fee; these are pure Arc gas at about 25 Gwei. Each transaction has a fixed base (about 21,000 gas) that batching shares, so the base per game falls as N grows (at N=100 it is about 0.0000084 USDC, negligible). But each game also carries its OWN payload and its OWN 2 player signatures, and that per-game gas cannot be shared: measured handover is about 24,000 + N x 10,000 gas, settle about 23,000 + N x 18,000 gas, so about 28,000 gas per game is irreducible (handover event data + calldata, plus 2 ecrecover at about 3,000 gas each). That floors the per-game cost at about 28,000 x 25 Gwei = 0.0007 USDC, about 1,400 games per 1 USD. So batching more games cannot go below about 1,400 while we anchor PER GAME.

THE RIDICULOUSLY CHEAP TIER IS PER SESSION, NOT PER GAME (owner 2026-09-23): to go far below 1,400 games/$1, stop anchoring each game and anchor the SESSION instead. Open ONE session (or one event handover), play MANY games inside it for free on the Foskaay GGI Midchain, and settle ONCE with a single Merkle root / rolling digest over all the games. Then the on-chain cost is one handover + one settle for N games, so per game is about 0.0017/N: N=100 gives about 0.000017 USDC (about 58,000 games/$1), N=1,000 about 580,000 games/$1. This is the v5 'open once, free inside, settle once' model, and it needs NO new core function: the existing sealFinal already accepts a digest, so the client can pass a Merkle root. The Foskaay GGI explorer proves each game by replaying its signed move log against the on-chain root. Three tiers, all optional: (1) per-game on-chain board about 10 games/$1; (2) per-game event Foskaay GGI Midchain floor about 1,400 games/$1; (3) per-session Foskaay GGI Midchain about 58,000+ games/$1.

NULLIFIER TRADE-OFF (owner 2026-09-23): the approved event-based core plan included a nullifier mapping (sessionId => settled) to stop double settlement. Measured, that mapping costs one SSTORE per settle (about 20,000 gas = about 0.0004 USDC per game), which would roughly raise the per-game event floor from about 0.0007 to about 0.0011 and drop it from about 1,400 to about 900 games/$1. It may be unnecessary: the settle digest is deterministic and every settle must carry the players' valid signatures, so a replay only re-emits an IDENTICAL event (idempotent and harmless) and a DIFFERENT result is impossible without the players' signatures. Recommendation: ship the event-based functions WITHOUT the nullifier (purely additive, no storage change, no migration, no version bump, cheapest), and document the reasoning; add the nullifier later only if a concrete duplicate-record problem appears. This is the one decision to confirm before the live upgrade.

PER-SESSION TIER MEASURED + CORE UPGRADED (owner-approved, 2026-09-23): (a) TIER 3 MEASURED: anchoring the SESSION (one handover + one settle carrying a Merkle root over N games and 2 signatures) keeps both transactions FLAT (handover 0.000782, settle 0.000930) no matter how many games are inside, so per game = 0.001712/N: N=3 gives 1,753 games/$1, N=5 2,920, N=10 5,841, N=100 58,411. This is the ridiculously cheap tier and the pitch headline. (b) CORE UPGRADED: event-based handover/handoverMany/settle/settleMany/midchainDigest added to the EXISTING SessionRegistry proxy via a UUPS logic upgrade, same address 0x5165809149Be8A72c72EedBa6a13d57014Ba1bE5, new implementation 0x05D492C0Cc4e890131c163b302Ab20B56542D2B2. ADDITIVE ONLY: no storage change, no gap change, no version bump, no migration; after the upgrade feeRecipient/operator/version/nonces/gameStateOf were all verified identical and midchainDigest answers on the proxy. No nullifier (owner decision, see above). Tests: test/SessionRegistryMidchain.t.sol (7 tests); 155/155 forge tests pass. SDK helpers added (handover/handoverMany/settleMidchain/settleMidchainMany/midchainDigest/signMidchain/verifyMidchain), versions bumped to 0.1.5; republish + browser bundle regeneration is the remaining step.

CLEAN 2-CONTRACT CORE, FRESH DEPLOY + SDK 0.2.0 (owner-approved, 2026-09-23): the rail is now exactly TWO upgradeable contracts, OpenZeppelin-only, no legacy. SessionRegistry: handover/handoverMany (PAYABLE; the fee is forwarded to the vault in the same transaction), settle/settleMany (OpenZeppelin ECDSA.recover), midchainDigest, and FREE pure random/randomN. FeeVault: native-USDC fee, deposit callable ONLY by the SessionRegistry, owner withdraw (OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard). FEE ENFORCEMENT: handover requires the fee and settle refuses unless FeeVault.paid(sessionId), so the fee sits inside the functions a dev must call and cannot be skipped on the official core. REMOVED with no legacy: SessionState, Randomness, BatchedSettlement, the on-chain-board port (GeneralsGame) and the superseded prototype; batching needs no contract (the settle carries a Merkle root) and randomness is a free pure function. FRESH UUPS PROXIES on Arc testnet: SessionRegistry 0xb0A5A2D316bEEd2f75786cb60bfa2256C52281eE (impl 0x3cE48a010B17ef038E45F43e5f4cAef6358aA049), FeeVault 0x9EE0b4c1622C5f2B7710b1fe4Ec2Be86833aDe39 (impl 0x13800e1dd0319622a1Ac4Dc2D4896F3DcabA58fc); fee 0.001 native USDC/session; wiring verified on-chain. OpenZeppelin vendored (v5.x exact closure): OwnableUpgradeable, ContextUpgradeable, ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable, ECDSA. SDK republished: @foskaay/ggi-contracts-sdk 0.2.0 (renamed from @foskaay/ggi-contracts, now deprecated) + @foskaay/ggi-sdk 0.2.0 (handover/handoverMany/settle/settleMany/createSessionKey/signMove/verifyMove/random/randomN/fee/isPaid), browser bundle regenerated, clean-install outsider test PASS. 23/23 forge tests pass.

FRESH CORE RENAME + 3-PART FEE, ARC TESTNET (owner-approved 2026-09-26, Phase 1): the core is FRESH, not an in-place upgrade. The contract formerly named SessionRegistry is renamed to the LOCKED name FoskaayGGI and deployed behind a NEW UUPS proxy (permanent) at 0x793785CE66992211B7c60dFCf0318869678D33a4 (impl 0x6A7cF5Db0Df5d5Ae8D181A10BFfa9a0Eb2438017), version 2, still OpenZeppelin only and upgradeable. It adds the CONFIG-DRIVEN 3-part session fee (feeBase 0.0004 + feePerAccount 0.0004 + feePerGame 0.0002, native USDC, charged once at connect; only the per-game part grows with batching; nothing inside the Foskaay GGI Midchain is charged) and handoverWithAccounts(..., address[] accounts, uint16 games) which records the dev-declared lifted accounts of ANY count plus the game count. The legacy single-fee handover/handoverMany are UNCHANGED. Names are LOCKED (owner): core FoskaayGGI, game FoskaayGGIGames, player FoskaayGGIPlayers (Phase 2). The demo game FoskaayGGILudo is untouched until Phase 2. Tests: foskaay-ggi 37/37 forge tests pass. Address propagated to the SDK, contracts package, explorer, docs, relay and deployment records.

FRESH GAME + PLAYER ACCOUNTS, ARC TESTNET (owner-approved 2026-09-26, Phase 2): FoskaayGGIGames (proxy 0x24e38ac2e80958782a8Bc5CD479bbe2e5D81EcDF, impl 0x83418a85B88a44859F95E321F2089fEd503f45d3) holds the match on-chain (Game struct: turn, seats, step, board bytes, boardHash, over) plus the Ludo pure rules that run free in the Foskaay GGI Midchain, and settle(sessionId, Game[] list, address[] seatPlayers, bytes32 gameTag) writes N games in ONE tx and calls FoskaayGGIPlayers.credit(...) in the same step (points decoded from each board's embedded per-seat points; settle is owner-gated so points cannot be minted). FoskaayGGIPlayers (proxy 0x1614ebc72eA1cB3D31975b3976B5B474FAcE3b3C, impl 0xbEA1DE7d6F80f57C13e5840c8957a6C3Fd5BbACd) holds per player, per game tag points/lives/records; credit/setLives/addRecord are callable ONLY by its game (or owner for a repair); pointsOf/livesOf/recordOf. Both FRESH UUPS proxies, OpenZeppelin only, version 1, permanent, wired (players.game = games, games.players = players; setGame tx 0x12aa79d03ead322e7018fdc1d9b8654ca162155befbe501a4bb2664918b6bfc7). The legacy FoskaayGGILudo (pure rules only) stays deployed untouched until the frontend moves over in Phase 5. Tests: foskaay-ggi 46/46 forge tests pass (9 new). sections.heading: The three layers this achieves
bullets: On-chain (truth): the contract stores the session, the start hash and the final hash, and settles. Nothing can settle unless the signatures and the hash chain are valid.

Foskaay GGI Midchain (free play): every move is a signed, hash-chained message run through the game's pure rules via eth_call. Free for the player AND free for the sponsor. Players, seats, moves, rewards, lives, timer and points all survive here as opaque data the game's rules read and write.
Off-chain (render only): the frontend draws the board; Vercel holds the sponsor key and submits only the handover and settle transactions. Neither owns the truth.

sections.heading: Honest limits
bullets: The chain does not see moves live, only the two endpoints. A third party can verify by replaying the signed moves; mid-session reads come from the untrusted relay cache.
Settle needs the players' final signatures. If a player vanishes we need a timeout or forfeit rule (MagicBlock has turn clocks; we would need the same).
The game's rules must be a deterministic pure function for the dispute path (no external calls).
PREVRANDAO is always 0 on Arc, so randomness comes from the commit-reveal seed plus the hash chain, never the block.

sections.heading: Why per-game batching floors at about 1,400 games per 1 USD (measured)
paragraphs: There is no hidden fee. These are pure Arc gas at about 25 Gwei. Every transaction has a fixed base of about 21,000 gas that batching shares, so the base per game shrinks as N grows (at N=100 it is about 0.0000084 USDC). But each game also carries its OWN payload and its OWN 2 player signatures, and that per-game gas cannot be shared. Measured: handover is about 24,000 + N x 10,000 gas and settle is about 23,000 + N x 18,000 gas, so about 28,000 gas per game is irreducible (event data plus calldata, plus 2 ecrecover at about 3,000 gas each). At 25 Gwei that is about 0.0007 USDC per game, about 1,400 games per 1 USD. Batching more games cannot beat that while we anchor PER GAME.

rows: one handover + one settle per game
one handover + one settle for N games (Merkle root)

bullets: Tier 3 is the ridiculously cheap one, and it needs NO new core function: the existing sealFinal accepts a digest, so the client passes a Merkle root over the games' final hashes. The moves inside the session are free on the Foskaay GGI Midchain, and the Foskaay GGI explorer proves each game by replaying its signed move log against the on-chain root.
All three tiers are optional. A dev picks the tier that fits: instant per-game on-chain proof, cheap per-game events, or maximum cheapness per session.

Nullifier trade-off: an SSTORE per settle costs about 20,000 gas (about 0.0004 USDC per game), which would raise tier 2 from about 1,400 to about 900 games/$1. It is likely unnecessary (the digest is deterministic and valid player signatures are required, so replay is idempotent and a different result is impossible). Recommendation: ship without it, purely additive.

rules: arcv2m1 never calls arcv2m4: the game and rewards are separated. The game emits into the seam (arcv2m2) and knows nothing about how points work.

UNIVERSAL SEAM (arcv2m2) is the ONLY way out of a game: every game ends with the same call (window.publishGameResult, gfg:game-result@1 envelope). arcv2m3/arcv2m4/arcv2m7 subscribe to the bus (window.onGameResult) and never read game internals. No game ships its own reward/competition plug.
arcv2m7 needs no arcv2m8: competitions stand alone from sponsor; escrow is an optional plugin.
Local (arcv2m3) never diluted: no multiplier, no purchase, no bonus, no giveaway, no referral on local points.
Multiplier only at arcv2m4 flow-up: 2x/3x/4x touches M4b lifetime + M4c spendable, never arcv2m3 or M4a.
Everything slots together by source tag ('Ludo', 'Ayo Olopon', 'signup_bonus', 'referral').
Modular + pluggable: each module is interchangeable and game-agnostic; no module is tailored to a single game.

Extensible: arcv2m1-arcv2m9 cover the current roadmap. Any genuinely new domain (community/forum, support, profile, etc.) becomes a NEW module (arcv2m10+) recorded here FIRST. A feature is never 'unmodular' - it either slots into an existing module or earns a new one.

LOCKED PER-GAME SPECS ARE THE BENCHMARK (arcv2m1A rule): each game under arcv2m1A (Ludo locked, Ayo Olopon planned, ...) has its own LOCKED spec in the arcv2m1 game dropdown - the source of truth for building AND testing that game. The agent reads it before/during the build, checks the result against it, and only concludes/commits/pushes arcv2m1 for that game when the build matches A-Z.

RPC/REGION-AGNOSTIC BUILD RULE (hard, locked 2026-08-18): every on-chain capability in ANY module MUST be RPC/region agnostic by construction. New per-player PDA types ship their own undelegate instruction in the same program build (so any account can leave a flaky/banned ER region and be re-pinned); client/relay/probe never hardcode one ER endpoint/region (resolve each account's hosting region from the Magic Router and target it; 3-region registry + failover is the base transport); delegate account maps use the relay's camelCase key form for #[delegate] helper accounts. Survived the 2026-08-18 US-route ban by re-pinning the fleet to AS. A banned region is a re-pin job, never a feature outage.

PREMIUM POINTS (arcv2m5) ARE THEIR OWN ECONOMY (locked 2026-08-20): premium_lifetime + premium_spendable live in the [gfgprem, player] PDA, acquired ONLY by direct purchase (admin/sponsor credit), never from gameplay, signup, referral, or giveaway. Premium spendable works wherever global spendable works PLUS places global NEVER can (subscription, lives). Premium never merges into global (arcv2m4) or local (arcv2m3) and never dilutes M4a pure.

SUBSCRIPTION STATE IS ON-CHAIN (locked 2026-08-20): subscription_level + active_until live in the premium PDA, never Supabase as truth. No auto-renew: a 30-day window lapses passively. Multiplier stays kind=1 at arcv2m4 flow-up only.

R12 COMPETITION INSTANCES ARE CONFIG, NOT CODE (owner 2026-08-22): games[], requirements (multi-select spendable families + tier level), entry cost, window, USD pool, prize shares, redemption and payout mode are DATA on an on-chain instance. Changing them = new instance params, never a code rewrite.

R13 COMPETITIONS ARE ON-CHAIN ONLY (owner 2026-08-22): no web2 db (Supabase) for the competition lifecycle - identity, requirements, window, pool, winners and paid status are on-chain, so sponsors can plug 30/70 rake + escrow (arcv2m8) later.

R14 PRIZES ARE USD/POINTS, REDEMPTION AGNOSTIC (owner 2026-08-22): pool value is USD cents ($1 = N1,500 = 500 pts at the $0.002/pt base, adjustable per instance without rebuild); redemption (naira now; points/crypto/merch later) is presentational only.

R17 FINAL-POINTS + LIVE-TIER RANKING (owner 2026-08-22): earn-competition winner position uses Final Points = Total Points in-window X live plan boostFactor (L3 1.5 / L2 1.0); the factor re-reads the CURRENT subscription at every render - a mid-window downgrade to an unqualifying level hides the player from the leaderboard immediately, a downgrade to a lower qualifying level drops the boost instantly, and players who do not resubscribe before the final freeze earn no position.
